resources.title: National Values
resources.description: Theme: OUR VALUES | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of values e.g. like and dislike 2. Levels of manifestation of values: - individual - society 3. Importance of values in the society e.g. unity cooperation, harmony 4. Factors that promote value system e.g. - consistency - trust - tolerance - fairness - integrity - commitment
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain what is meant by values; 2. mention some of values in the society e.g. co- operation, self- reliance, tolerance. 3. describe the Level of manifestations of values; 4. identify societal factors that promote good values.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads the students to find out meaning of values. 2. Uses case studies and contrived situations to guide students to analyze the importance and manifestations of values in the individual and the society. 3. Guides students to identify factors that promote good value system.

Students: 1. Find out the meaning of values. 2. Participate in class discussion. 3. Compile a list of wise sayings in the community that teach values. 4. Ask and answer questions
resources.resources: 1. Introductory texts on values and value systems. 2. Books on African proverbs and folk tales. 3. Moral Instructional books. 4. Posters and Cartoons.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of values; 2. mention two importance of values in the society; 3. explain the manifestation of values; 4. list three factors that promote good values.

resources.title: National Values: Honesty
resources.description: Theme: CIVIC EDUCATION JSS ONE | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of honesty 2. Attributes of honesty 3. Benefits of honesty 4. Consequences of dishonesty e.g. in examination malpractice, cheating, fraudulent practices etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of honesty; 2. state attributes of Honesty; 3. explain the benefits of honesty; 4. di.scuss the consequences of dishonesty.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides discussion on: - the meaning and attributes of honesty; - benefits of honesty and consequences of dishonesty 2. Arranges for a guest to talk to the students about honesty; 3. Guides students role- play to demonstrate honest behaviour

Students: 1. Contribute to class discussion. 2. Role play to demonstrate honesty. 3. Recount instances that honesty paid off. 4. Write short story on the value of honesty 5. Listen to guest talks, ask and answer questions.
resources.resources: 1. Books on Moral Instructions 2. Dictionary 3. Newspaper stories 4. Documentaries 5. Posters and Cartoons.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of honesty; 2. list two attributes of honesty; 3. enumerate three benefits of honesty; 4. describe two consequences of dishonesty.

resources.title: National Values: Cooperation
resources.description: Theme: CIVIC EDUCATION JSS ONE | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of cooperation e.g. work together to achieve goal 2. Attributes e.g. sharing, caring, supporting etc. 3. Factors that promote cooperation: e.g. trust, setting goals together, patience, understanding, humility, tolerance, open-mindedness etc. 4. Benefits of cooperation - harmony - progress - goal achievement
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain cooperation; 2. describe the attributes of cooperation; 3. identify factors that promote cooperation, trust, humility, patience, tolerance, open mindedness; 4. state the benefits of cooperation.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads discussion on the meaning, attributes and benefits of cooperation. 2. Guides students in team activities. 3. Guides students to identify factors that promote cooperation. 4. Arranges for a guest speaker to talk to the students about cooperation.

Students: 1. Contribute to discussion and give examples. 2. Write essays on cooperation. 3. Relate their experiences in team activities. 4. Carry out group assignment and write report
resources.resources: 1. Films, newspapers, radio and TV programmes, dictionary, documentaries on ECOWAS, AU, UNO, Commonwealth Olympic games etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain cooperation and give two examples; 2. list three attributes of cooperation; 3. mention four factors that promote cooperation; 4. enumerate three benefits of cooperation.

resources.title: National Values: Self Reliance
resources.description: Theme: CIVIC EDUCATION JSS ONE | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of Self Reliance 2. Attributes of self-reliance 3. Processes of Identifying, Nurturing and Perfection of Talents and Skills. 4. Benefits of Self Reliance to • Oneself • Family • Society 5. Understanding that the wealth of a nation is contained in its natural and human resources. 6. Consequences of undiscovered talents and undeveloped skills.
resources.objectives: Student should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of self-reliance, 2. identify importance of self-reliance: 3. identify processes of discovering one's natural talents; 4. discuss how to nurture the identified talents; 5. mention the consequences of wasted talents and undeveloped skills.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussions on meaning, attributes and benefits of self- reliance. 2. Gives practical examples of agencies that help tap and develop talents. 3. Creates activities to help identify student skills and talents.

Students: 1. Contribute to discussion what they think their talents are and why people should be self- reliant. 2. Discuss possible areas of specialization and how to make wealth and develop the nation.
resources.resources: 1. Introductory textbooks on self reliance. 2. Visit to practical skills acquisition centres. 3. Practical activities to enable students identify their skills and talents.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define self- reliance; 2. discuss three benefits of self- reliance; 3. discuss two consequences of being dependent on others or society; 4. identify the importance of Self-reliance; 5. enumerate five natural talents that people possess.

resources.title: Citizenship.
resources.description: Theme: CITIZENSHIP | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of citizenship Membership of a Nation based on laid down conditions. 2. Types of citizenship by birth, by registration and naturalization. 3. Process of becoming a citizen of a country.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of citizenship; 2. name different types of citizenship; 3. describe the processes of becoming citizen of a country.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to explain meaning and types of citizenship 2. Guides students' discussion on processes of becoming citizen of a country.

Students: 1. Find out and report on: - the birth places of their parents - their places of birth. 2. Explain differences between place of birth and place of origin.
resources.resources: 1. The Nigeria Constitution. 2. Specimen copy of citizenship registration forms. 3. Sample National I.D. Cards. 4. Sample Birth certificate.
resources.assessment: Student to: 1. describe the term, citizenship. 2. explain the concept of citizenship. 3. name two different types of citizenship. 4. explain two processes of becoming citizen of a country.

resources.title: Rights and Duties of Citizens
resources.description: Theme: CITIZENSHIP | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of rights and duties with examples: - right to education - right to life - right to opinion/ freedom of expression 2. Differences between "Rights" (e.g. voting rights) and "Duties" (e.g. payment of taxes, obedience to the law) of citizens. 3. Importance of citizens’ rights and duties - social control - peace - due process - discipline.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of rights and duties 2. identify and distinguish between citizen's rights and duties. 3. state the importance of citizen's rights and duties.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Prepares flash cards 2. Guides student to - Discuss the school rules and identify their rights and duties to the school - State the importance of rights and duties.

Students: 1. Read about citizens’ right and duties 2. Participate in class discussion and debates 3. Sort-out flash card on rights and duties
resources.resources: 1. School rules and regulations 2. The Nigerian Constitution 3. Flash cards
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of rights and duties of citizens 2. distinguish between Rights and Duties 3. give two examples of citizens’ rights and duties 4. mention three importance of rights and duties of citizens

resources.title: Objects for National Consciousness
resources.description: Theme: NATIONAL CONSCIOUSNESS AND IDENTITY | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES | Content: 1. National symbols - Coat of arms - National flag - National currency 2. National Anthem and Pledge. . 3. Purpose of establishment of National institutions like NYSC, Unity Schools, Federal Character etc. 4. Ways of promoting National Unity: - Tolerance, - Hospitality, - non- discrimination - inter-marriage etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify Nigeria's national symbols and their meanings; 2. describe the unifying measures included in the Nigerian national Anthem and pledge; 3. describe the measures adopted by government to promote unity among Nigerians; 4. discuss parts of the Nigerian Constitution that seek to promote national consciousness and national unity; 5. discuss how individuals and groups can promote national unity.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Brings pictures and charts to the classroom. 2. Guides the students to describe the features of national symbols and their meanings. 3. Analyses the national anthem and pledge and Identifies unifying national goals. 4. Discusses measures and institution that foster national unity among Nigerians. 5. Guides the students in identifying ways of promoting national unity.

Students: 1. Identify and describe national symbols. 2. Explain the meaning of the symbols. 3. Participate in class discussions. 4. Lead the discussion on how they can promote national unity.
resources.resources: 1. A chart showing all the Nigerian National symbols. 2. National flag 3. Specimen of Nigerian currency 4. Nigerian Constitution 5. Posters and Documentaries 6. Cartoons and films.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list three national symbols; 2. describe meaning of the features on the symbols; 3. identify the unifying factors in the National Anthem and Pledge; 4. discuss efforts by government to promote national ,unity; 5. discuss how individuals can promote national unity.

resources.title: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
resources.description: Theme: FUNDAMENTALS OF SOCIAL STUDIES EDUCATION JSS ONE | Sub-theme: FUNDAMENTALS OF SOCIAL STUDIES EDUCATION JSS ONE | Content: 1. History of Nigerian Social Studies Education: - First conceived in the united state and later spread to Europe. - After the world wars it was identified as a course that is relevant to the understanding of man and his problems. - Conferences were held to spread it in Africa, i.e. Mombasa conference in Kenya. - Back home in Nigeria, the Aiyetoro comprehensive High School Pilot Study and Project with the assistance of ford foundation. - Former twelve states of Nigeria went further to organize activities to promote social studies in their educational institution and schools. - In further development of the subject, many seminars and workshops have been organised by such bodies as the NERDC and Social Study Association of Nigeria (SOSAN) and others. - Today social studies is taught in the primary school, junior secondary schools, NTI, Grade II Teachers Certificates , Colleges of Education and Universities. One can obtain PhD in social studies.
resources.objectives: Student should be able explain the development of social studies Education in Nigeria.
resources.activities:
Teacher: Lead students to discuss the history of Nigerian Social Studies Education.

Students: Participate in discussion of history of Nigeria Social Studies Education.
resources.resources: 1. Students Textbooks. 2. Social Studies materials. 3. Resource persons. 4. Video clips, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to explain history of Nigerian Social Studies Education.

resources.title: Family as a Primary Social Group
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL STUDIES EDUCATION | Sub-theme: FUNDAMENTALS OF SOCIAL STUDIES EDUCATION JSS ONE | Content: 1. Meaning of Primary Social Group; It is a group whose members share close, personal, and long lasting relationships. Members show concern for one another, and share activities and culture. 2. What makes the Family a Primary Social Group - It is the main unit of socialization - Everybody belongs to one family or another - Every society grows from the social unit called family etc. 3. The roles and responsibilities of members of a family as a primary social group: - Get members to work for the growth of the community - Work as adult members to contribute to the economy - Play key roles in population growth, especially the father and mother - Play active role in political affairs e.g. registering and voting etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. Give a simple meaning of primary social group 2. Explain what makes the family a social group 3. Identify the roles and responsibilities of members of a family as a primary social group in the community
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides discussion on the meaning of primary social group. 2. Conducts a brainstorming session on what makes the family a primary social group. 3. Invites some parents to give talks on the roles and responsibilities of family members as a primary social group.

Students: 1. Participate in the guided discussion on the meaning of primary social group. 2. Provide a variety of responses during the brainstorming session. 3. Take notes and ask questions on the talk being given by the resource persons
resources.resources: 1. Relevant pictures and charts. 2. Charts for compiling responses during brainstormin g session. 3. Resource persons- parents
resources.assessment: 1. State the meaning of primary social group. 2. List any three things that make the family a primary social group. 3. List any three roles of members of the family as a primary group.

resources.title: The Consequences of Large/Small Family Size
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY AS THE BASIC UNIT OF SOCIETY | Sub-theme: FAMILY AS THE BASIC UNIT OF SOCIETY | Content: 1a. Characteristics of Large Family size- father, mother, and many children. 1b. Characteristics of Small Family Size- father, mother, and very few children. 2. Consequences of family size on: - quality of individual lives - the national economy
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. describe the characteristics of large family size and those of small family size 2. explain the consequences of family size on individual lives and the nation’s economy.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Illustrates the characteristics of large and small family sizes with posters, pictures and charts 2. Uses case studies to explain the consequences of family size

Students: 1. React to posters, picture and charts on the characteristics of large and small family sizes 2. Participate in discussions, and debates.
resources.resources: 1. Relevant posters, pictures and Charts, 2. Relevant cases 3. Documentaries on family life.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. Differentiate between a large family size and a small one. 2. List the consequences of large family size on: - the quality of life of the people and - the nation’s economy.

resources.title: Meaning and Characteristics of Culture
resources.description: Theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Sub-theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of Culture- a total way of life of the people. 2. Components of culture - Material and non material culture 3. Features of culture - Language - Food and dressing - Religion - Technology/ Craft, etc. 4. Characteristics of culture - We learn culture - It tells us how different activities can be carried out - It allows a range of permissible behaviours etc. 5. Cultural differences in Nigeria.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define culture 2. list the components of culture. 3. group the components of culture as material and non material. 4. state the characteristics of culture.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains culture with concrete examples. 2. Take students to the museum and places of cultural interest to observe the display of Nigerian culture. 3. Guides students to discuss and identify : - components of culture. - material and non-material culture. - characteristics of culture. - the uniqueness of Nigerian culture. 4. Organizes cultural activities and displays of cultural artifacts

Students: 1. Ask and answer questions on culture. 2. Observe and report Nigeria’s cultural heritage. 3. Participate in class discussions. 4. Collect and display materials from the various Nigerian cultures in cultural activities.
resources.resources: 1. Motion pictures of culture. 2. Pictures of cultural display. 3. Visits to museum 4. Regalia.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give a simple meaning of culture. 2. list components of Nigerian culture. 3. state some examples of material and non-material aspects of culture. 5. List characteristics of culture.

resources.title: Similarities and Differences among Cultures in Nigeria
resources.description: Theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Sub-theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Content: 1. Cultural similarities in Nigeria. 2. Cultural differences in Nigeria. 3. Shared Norms and Values of Nigerian Communities.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify cultural similarities among Nigerians. 2. identify cultural differences among Nigerians 3. mention some shared norms and values of Nigerian communities.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to identify variety of cultural traits among the different Nigerian cultures in order to identify their similarities. 2. Leads students to identify cultural differences among Nigerians. 3. Sets students on inquiry session to find out from the community areas some of the norms and values shared by Nigerian ethnic groups.

Students: 1. Participate in the identification of the variety of cultures to get the similarities 2. Identify differences in the cultures of Nigerians. 3. Participate in the inquiry session and report their findings to the class for further discussion on the cultural similarities among Nigerians.
resources.resources: 1. Motion pictures of culture. 2. Pictures of cultural display. 3. Regalia.
resources.assessment: Students to; 1. identify the similarities among the cultural groups around their locality. 2. identify the differences among the cultural ethnic groups around their locality. 3. mention some shared norms and values of Nigerian communities.

resources.title: Agents and Processes of Socialization
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL STUDIES EDUCATION JS ONE | Sub-theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of socialization- lifelong process of inheriting and passing on the norms, customs and ideologies of a social group. It may provide the individual with the skills and habits necessary for participating within their own society. 2. Agents of socialization e.g. family, school, religious organizations, press, age grade, peer group, clubs & societies. 3. Importance of socialization- is the means by which human infants begin to acquire the skills necessary to perform as a functioning member of their society, and is the most important learning process one can experience
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define socialization. 2. enumerate the agents of socialization. 3. mention the importance of socialization
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads a discussion on the meaning of socialization. 2. Guides and directs students to role-play socialization models. 3. Uses futures wheel exercise to discuss the importance of socialization in our community.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussion. 2. Role-play Agent of socialization in class. 3. Provide responses to complete the future wheel on the importance of socialization in our community.
resources.resources: 1. Charts on socialization models. 2. Role cards. 3. Product of futures wheel exercise.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the meaning of socialization. 2. list some of the agents of socialization. 3. Mention the importance of socialization.

resources.title: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
resources.description: Theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES JSS ONE | Sub-theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES JSS ONE | Content: 1. Structure and Process of Forming Road Safety Club in Schools 2. The Roles of Road Safety Club in the Socialization of Youths:
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. describe the structure and process of forming Road Safety Club 2. state the roles of Road Safety Club in the socialization of youths.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents charts on the structure and process of forming of Road Safety Club for class discussion. 2. Invites road safety corp officer to give talks on the roles of FRSC in the socialization of youth

Students: 1. Draw the organogram of Road Safety Club and discuss it. 2. Write down the key points of the talk on the roles of Road Safety in the Socialization of the Youths.
resources.resources: 1. A copy of Road Safety Club guidelines. 2. A picture of Road Safety Club member(s).
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. Describe the structure and process of formation of Road Safety Club in schools from an organogram. 2. state the roles of Road Safety Club in the socialization of youths.

resources.title: Common Social Problems in Nigeria
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Contemporary social problems in Nigeria (e.g. - Exam malpractice; Cultism, HIV/AIDS) etc.). 2. Causes of contemporary social problems in Nigeria e.g. poverty, corruption, lack of parental care, greed etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify social problems in the Nigerian society. 2. discuss the causes of the social problems.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Involves students in a pre-lesson identification of contemporary social problems by noting 1. the frequency of occurrence of the problems on print and electronic media. 2. Guides class to discuss social problems and their causes.

Students: 1. Collate and report information on contemporary social problems. 2. Participate in class discussion social problems and their causes.
resources.resources: 1. Newspapers and magazine articles. 2. Radio, TV and internet options.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list common social problems in Nigeria giving examples from their communities. 2. discuss the causes of common social problems in Nigeria.

resources.title: Ways of Solving Common Social Problems in Nigeria.
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Effects of social problems; Poverty; underdevelopment; etc. 2. Ways of solving contemporary social problems e.g. Government policies, participation in civil society, personal discipline e.g. contentment, loyalty, faithfulness etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the effects of social issues and problems in Nigeria. 2. evaluate the measures adopted to solve social problems.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads a discussion on the effects of social problems. 2. Guides students on ways of solving the social issues/problems.

Students: 1. Discuss the effects of social problems. 2. Mention ways of solving the common social problems in their communities.
resources.resources: 1. Newspapers and magazine articles. 3. Radio, TV and internet. 3. Documentaries
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. Explain current social problems. 2. Proffer adequate measures for overcoming the problems.

resources.title: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community 1.
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Need for safety. 2. Safety measures in the Home, school and workplaces. 3. Safety guidelines for pedestrians, cyclists, motor cyclists, motorists, Etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 2. 1. explain the need 3. for safety. 4. 5. 2. enumerate 6. measures that 7. could be taken to 8. ensure safety in 9. the home, school, 10. workplace and 11. the environment, 3. list safety guidelines for pedestrians, cyclists, motorists,
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to explain the needs and measures for ensuring safety in an environment. 3. Lists safety guidelines for pedestrians e.g. Walking on the left hand side facing on - coming vehicle. - Wearing bright coloured material while walking in the night etc. 4. Demonstrates safety guidelines for road- crossing. 5. Identifies safety guidelines for cyclists and motor-cyclists e.g.: 6. a. use of safety helmets b. use of rider’s protection e.g. padded clothes, bright coloured jacket, etc. 7. Explains safety guidelines for motorists e.g. - Use of seat belts - Obeying all traffic regulations - Ensure proper vehicle maintenance.

Students: 1. Listen to guest speaker ask and answer questions. 2. Explain the need for safety. 3. Mention safety measures in the home, school and environment. 4. List safety guidelines for pedestrians, cyclists and motorists,
resources.resources: 1. Newspapers and magazine articles. 2. Radio and TV and internet. 3. Documentaries
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the need for safety. 2. mention their roles in promoting safety in their homes and schools. 3. enumerate safety measures that could be taken to ensure safety in homes, schools, and workplaces.

resources.title: Common Crimes, Causes and Effects.
resources.description: Theme: COMMON CRIMES AND SECURITY MANAGEMENT 1 | Sub-theme: COMMON CRIMES AND SECURITY MANAGEMENT 1 | Content: 1. Examples of crimes: e.g. -Falsehood -Theft -Rape -Murder -advance fee fraud- (419) -sale of contaminated food -dealing in fake drugs, etc. 2. Causes and effects of common crimes 3. Crime prevention: - cooperation with security agents, school and neighbourhood authorities in crime
resources.objectives: Students should be able to : 1. identify common crimes. 2. state the causes of common crimes. 3. mention the effects of common crimes. 4. report appropriately ways of relating with security agents. 5. explain ways of relating with security agents, school and neighborhood authorities in crime prevention. 6. avoid criminal behaviours.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to identify common crimes. 2. Leads students to state the causes of common crimes 3. Asks pupils to mention the effects of common crimes 4. Guides students to find out more information on ways of relating with security agents, school, and neighborhood authorities in crime prevention.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussion leading to identifying causes and effects of common crimes. 2. State causes of common crimes 3. Mention effects of common crimes 4. State ways of relating with security agents, school and neighborhood authorities in crime prevention.
resources.resources: Textbooks, charts, Video clips, Stickers Posters, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify common crimes. 2. mention the causes of common crimes. 3. state the effects of common crimes 4. state ways of relating with security agents, school, neighborhood authorities in crime prevention

resources.title: National Values: Integrity
resources.description: Theme: OUR VALUES JSS TWO | Sub-theme: COMMON CRIMES AND SECURITY MANAGEMENT 1 | Content: 1. Meaning of integrity 2. Attributes of integrity - probity, honesty - contentment - truthfulness - fair-play - non-compromise of principles etc. 3. Examples of people of integrity in the society. 4. Need for people of integrity in the society e.g. community development, peaceful co- existence models for the young ones etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of integrity; 2. describe attributes of people of integrity; 3. discuss the need to have people of integrity in the society.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides discussion on - meaning of integrity - Importance of integrity; - Consequences of lack of integrity. 2. Reads the citation of people of integrity and guides students to identify the special attributes of the people. 3. Guides students to compile folklore that teach the consequences of lack of integrity.

Students: 1. Contribute to discussion, ask questions and take notes. 2. Identify people of integrity in their community, write essays defending their claims. 3. Compile folklores on integrity.
resources.resources: 1. Textbooks 2. newspapers 3. magazines 4. biographies 5. documentaries 6. folklore 7. citations 8. -cartoons
resources.assessment: Student to: 1. explain the meaning of integrity; 2. state two attributes of integrity; 3. describe importance of having people of integrity in the community, 4. list two people of integrity in the community with justification.

resources.title: National values: Contentment
resources.description: Theme: OUR VALUES JSS TWO | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES JSS TWO | Content: 1. Meaning of contentment. 2. Attributes of Contentment: - satisfaction - lack of envy - rejections of greed and corruption - humility, etc. 3. Effects of lack of contentment on society: - corruption - greed - envy - theft - prostitution - robbery - cheating, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of contentment; 2. describe the attributes of contentment; 3. identify the consequences of lack of contentment.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to explain the meaning of contentment. 2. Asks students to compile local sayings, adage and proverbs that promote contentment. 3. Guides the students to dramatize the effects of lack of contentment in the society. 4. Organize. guest talk on lack of contentment.

Students: 1. Attend and listen to guest talk. 2. Participate in discussion/ask question and write notes. 3. Identify effects of lack of contentment on the society. carry out assignment of compiling local sayings, proverbs etc to promote contentment.
resources.resources: 1. Textbooks 2. Moral Instructional books 3. Corrupt Practices and other Related Offences Act 2000 4. Cartoons
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of contentment; 2. list three attributes of contentment; 3. list two adages and proverbs to support contentment; 4. state three consequences of lack of contentment.

resources.title: National Values: Discipline
resources.description: Theme: OUR VALUES JSS TWO | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES JSS TWO | Content: 1. Meaning of Discipline 2. Attributes of discipline - self control - moderation - modesty - respect for le gitimate authority - respect for rule and regulations - perseverance - dedication, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of discipline; 2. list the attributes of a disciplined person; 3. state the benefits of disciplined behaviour; 4. discuss the consequences of indiscipline on the individual and the society.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides discussion on: - the meaning of discipline - attributes of discipline; - benefits of disciplined behaviour; - consequences of undisciplined behaviour 2. Asks students to narrate personal experiences that demonstrates some attributes of discipline and consequences of indiscipline.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussions, ask questions, answer questions, take notes. 2. Narrate personal experiences on disciplined and undisciplined behaviour. 3. Role-play some attributes of discipline. 4. Write notes on discipline in school and the community. 5. Participate in development of check-list.
resources.resources: 1. Books 2. Posters 3. cartoons 4. Relevant publications 5. School rules and regulation 6. Dictionary
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define discipline; 2. state three attributes of discipline; 3. enumerate three benefits of discipline; 4. state two consequences of indiscipline.

resources.title: National Values: Courage
resources.description: Theme: OUR VALUES JSS TWO | Sub-theme: OUR VALUES JSS TWO | Content: 1. Meaning of courage e.g. exercise boldness in carrying out positive activities in community. 2. types of courage - physical courage (the willingness to exercise physical energy to get things done) - - moral courage (the ability to choose to do what is right irrespective of pressure to do otherwise) - spiritual courage (courage to exhibit ones spiritual faith and live according to its tenets); 3. Attributes of courageous persons - commitment - endurance - determination - steadfastness - diligence - boldness - bravery etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of courage 2. identify types of courage (physical, moral and religious). 3. state the attributes of a courageous individual/ society.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to: - explain the meaning of courage; - list types of courage and explain their meaning 2. Guides discussion on demonstrations of different types of courage. 3. Invites guest lecturers from relevant agencies e.g. ICPC, EFCC, Police etc. on the need for moral courage.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussion, ask questions and write notes. 2. Listen to stories of courageous actions by heroes and heroines in their community. 9. Write notes on courageous steps taken in school. 10. Participate in guest lectures.
resources.resources: 1. Books 2. Pictures of heroes 3. Biographies 4. Recorded Radio and TV Programmes. 5 .Documentaries 6. Home videos 7. Newspaper Report 8. Posters 9. cartoons
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of courage; 2. list three types of courage; 3. state four attributes of courageous individuals in the society; 4. list two examples of class monitors that have taken courageous steps.

resources.title: Nigeria as a Federation
resources.description: Theme: GOVERANCE JSS TWO | Sub-theme: GOVERANCE JSS TWO | Content: 1. Meaning of Federation 2. Needs for Federation; - National Integration - Unity in diversity - Controlling activities of states 3. Characteristics of a Federation: - sharing of powers between Central and State Government - States have constitutionally defined control over their own affairs - Central Government control the States - Constitution of Federal system
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of Federation; 2. explain the needs for Federation and federal systems; 3. describe the characteristics of a Federation.

Factors responsible for children and women trafficking - False hope of continuing education or working abroad - Poverty - Increasing demand for foreign workers - Growth of billion-dollar sex and entertainment industry etc 3. Consequences of human trafficking: - Loss of human resources - Life of crime, addiction and sexual violence - Weakens ties of family love and influence etc. 4. Preventive measures: - Awareness raising - Education, - Advocacy, Legislation, etc.
resources.objectives: Student should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of human trafficking; 2. highlight the factors responsible for children and women trafficking; 3. state the social consequences of children and women trafficking; 4. suggest possible ways of preventing human trafficking
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses debate and brain storming to elicit responses from students on: - The meaning of human trafficking - Factors responsible for children and women trafficking; - Consequences of trafficking in women and children. 2. Invites a guest speaker to give a talk on human trafficking prevention. 3. Constitutes mock courts where students try children and women traffickers.

Students: 1. Participate actively in discussions and debates 2. Listen to guest speaker, take notes and ask questions from the resource person and the teacher.
resources.resources: 1. Poster 2. Video/ film Clips 3. Resource Person 4. Charts; etc
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of human trafficking; 2. Outline five factors responsible for children and women trafficking, 3. State any five consequences of trafficking in children and women;. 4. suggest ways of preventing human trafficking

resources.title: Harmful Traditional Practices
resources.description: Theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Sub-theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of harmful traditional Practices- Practices that bring physical, mental, social and health dangers, and damages to people. 2. Examples of harmful traditional practices - Use of children for begging - Child agric labour - Female circumcision - Early marriage etc. 3. Consequences: - Problem at child birth - Exploitation of children - Deprivation of schooling - VVF etc. 4. Preventing of harmful traditional practices - Public Enlightenment
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of harmful traditional practices; 2. describe different types of harmful traditional practices in Nigerian/ communities 3. suggest measures to prevent and stop harmful traditional practices in Nigeria/ communities.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to explain harmful traditional practices 2. Acts as a facilitator and collates learning experiences 3. Uses storytelling and enter-educate method to guide students to identify human traditional practices in Nigeria. 4. Uses problem- solving approach, mock courts, and contrived situations to illustrate the con- sequences of these practices and ways of eradicating them.

Students: 1 . Find out about harmful traditional p r a c t i c e s i n t h e ir communities from their parents and old people around them and report to the class. 2. Participate in discussions on traditional practices. 3. Actively participate in problem solving activities, mock courts etc.
resources.resources: - Relevant literature/ documents (e.g. the constitution, international and local agreement on human rights), - Art works and drawings - Films and videos, - Photographs - Posters - Charts
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the term harmful traditional practices; 2. list any four harmful traditional practices in Nigeria; 3. analyze the consequences of these practices; 4. describe measurers that could be taken to eradicate these practices in Nigeria.

resources.title: Promoting Peaceful Living in our Society
resources.description: Theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Sub-theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Content: 1. Meaning of Peace- cordial and friendly living among different groups of people. 2. Types: - Positive peace - Negative/ uneasy peace 3. Importance of peace: - Lack of violent conflict - Progress and development - Happiness and less stress etc. 4. Ways of promoting peace: - tolerance - social justice - human rights, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of peace; 2. explain the importance of living in peace with one another; 3. describe ways of promoting peace in our society.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses guided questions to lead students to find out meaning and types of peace; 2. Organises debate with students on the importance of living in peace with one another; 3. Guide students to role play the importance of peaceful living after the debate; 4. Invite a senior police officer to come and give talk on the various ways of promoting peace in our society.

Students: 1. Participate in the guided class discussions; 2. Active involvement in the debate; 3. Role playing 4. Listen to, take notes and ask questions on the talk.
resources.resources: 1. Picture and chart of people living together peacefully. 2. Resource Person 3. Role cards. 4. TV /Radio 5. Drama and Songs
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of peace 2. differentiate between types of peace 3. state the importance of peace; 4. describe with examples those ways that can promote peace

resources.title: Social Conflicts
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Meaning of Conflict as Inter personal misunderstanding. 2. Types of conflict - Non-violent - Violent 3. Examples of Conflict; - inter-ethnic conflicts e.g. Urhobo/Itsekiri, Kataf/Hausa, Yoruba/Hausa Conflicts etc. - Communal/Intra ethnic e.g. Ife/ Modakeke, Agulaeri/Umuleri 4. Causes and consequences of Conflicts.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to:- 1. explain the meaning of conflict; 2. outline the various types of conflicts 3. discuss the causes of conflicts. 4. explain the consequences of Conflicts.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of conflict to the students after dramatic presentation of rowdy scene. 2. Uses simulations to guide students to identify types and examples of conflict. 3. Leads students to recognize General Consequences of Violent conflicts.

Students: 1. Dramatize a rowdy scene to illustrate the meaning, causes and consequences of conflicts. 2. Participate in discussion and simulations on issue.
resources.resources: 1. Chart and pictures of Stressful environment. 2. Pictures showing destruction as a result of violent conflicts. 3. Simulation 4. Radio and TV 5. Documentaries of conflict situations. 6. Drama/songs.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define conflict; 2. identify types of conflicts. 3. list examples of conflicts. 4. explain the causes of conflict. 5. state the con sequences of conflicts.

resources.title: Managing and Resolving.
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Conflict management and resolution e.g. dialogue, compromise, arbitration, court rulings, mediation etc. 2. Attributes required for conflict resolution: - mutual understanding - -respect for rule of law - -tolerance in the face of provocation - -self control - -respect for opposing views.
resources.objectives: Students should be able: 1. suggest non- violent methods of resolving Conflicts. 2. explain that resolution of conflicts enhances national peaceful coexistence.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to explain conflict resolution. 2. Demonstrates non- violent means of conflict resolution. 3. Organizes visits to courts, Alternative Disputes Resolution Centers (ADR) 4. Organises guest lectures on Conflict Resolution

Students: 1. Ask relevant questions during lessons. 2. Observe Courts and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) in session.
resources.resources: 1. Radio and TV Documentaries of conflict situations. 2. Drama/songs.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. describe non- violent methods of resolving conflicts 2. explains that conflict resolution enhances natural peaceful co-existence.

resources.title: Controlling Cultism in our Society.
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Meaning of Cultism 2. Causes of Cultism - home background; - peer group influence; - exposure to foreign values; - proliferation of arms; - drug/ substance abuse - poor leadership; and - injustice/marginaliza tion. 3. Consequences of cultism: - violence; - break down of social values; - criminal tendencies; and - moral decadence 4. Solutions to cultism.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define cultism; 2. identify causes of cultism; 3. describe the consequences of cultism; 4. Proffer solutions to the problems of cultism in Nigeria.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to explain the meaning of cultism and discuss its causes. 2. Organizes a brain storming session on the causes of cultism. 3. Invites a guest speaker to discuss the consequences and solutions to cultism. 4. Encourages and guides students to listen to Radio and TV programmes that discuss cultism and its effects on individuals and society. 5. Directs students’ play- let on causes, consequences and ways of preventing cultism in our society.

resources.title: Preventing Drug Trafficking.
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Meaning of drug trafficking: 2. Reasons for Trafficking in Drugs - poverty; - ignorance; - Greed etc. 3. Consequences of drug Trafficking: - Bad image for the Country. - Imprisonment - Death Penalty in some cases - Forfeiture of assets (local and foreign) etc. 4. Prevention of drug trafficking - education - alleviation of poverty - legislation - International cooperation.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the meaning of drug trafficking; 2. identify reasons for trafficking in drugs; 3. describe the dangers of drug trafficking; 4. identify ways for preventing drug trafficking
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides the students to: - find out the meaning of drug trafficking - Identify reasons for drug trafficking. 2. Arranges for a guest talk on consequences of drug trafficking and solutions. 3. Takes students on visits to relevant agencies (NDLEA, EFCC, Police Stations, Prisons, Service Departments, etc.) to inquire and discuss drug trafficking, problems and suggest solutions.

Students: 1. Participate in discussions. 2. Listen to talks; take notes; ask and answer questions. 3. Go on excursions.
resources.resources: 1. Posters from NDLEA,EFCC, on drug trafficking; 2. Dictionary; 3. Newspapers; 4. Magazines; 5. Resource person 6. Cartoon; and 7. Documentary
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain drug trafficking and state reasons for it; 2. list the consequences of drug trafficking; 3. state some ways by which drug trafficking can be controlled or stopped.

Demonstration of awareness
